Subject: Capacity passport: throughput recap & next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our side plus concrete next steps so we can size a short pilot: 

Summary of requirements we heard (please correct where I mis-specified):
- Peak QPS: ~250 requests/sec (peaks driven by checkout bursts)
- Baseline QPS: ~18-25 rps (steady-state)
- Typical tokens per request: ~100–140 (avg ~120)
- Peak tokens/sec (aggregate): ~30k tokens/sec during 10–20s crests
- Streaming sessions: 180–210 concurrent long-lived streams (avg session length ~40s)
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms, target p50 ~120–150ms; firm business need is smooth checkout experience

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Alex — can you share a 72-hour sample of anonymized request headers or a small CSV with timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, and session_id? (we typically look for 1–3 days to understand crest shapes)
2) Marissa / Karthik — I’ll loop you in for a short technical deep-dive to confirm streaming concurrency assumptions and cost/throughput tradeoffs.
3) Proposed pilot: 2-week pilot (production-similar traffic replay) with a canary at ~50% traffic for the first day. If sizing looks good, we can propose a Dedicated reserved pool for predictable tail.

Attachments: stubbed pilot checklist and sample CSV schema (packly_token_sample.csv).

Schedule: propose Thu 2026-09-28 10:00 PT for a 45-minute sizing deep-dive — happy to adjust.

Thanks — Sean

Thanks Sean — added a couple quick technical clarifying questions before we pull a sizing config: 

Marissa's checklist (short):
- Token distribution: is the 120 avg driven by text-only responses or frequent tool calls? If tools are common, effective tokens-per-request can spike.
- Burst shape: are the 30k tokens/sec crests single-request dominated (many concurrent small requests) or single-session dominated (a few sessions with large multi-turn exchanges)?
- Sessionization: do session_id values persist across retries/refreshes, or are they ephemeral per websocket connection?
- Long-tail: what percent of requests are "long" (>500 tokens) vs short (<40 tokens)? Even 5–10% can change memory/kv-cache assumptions.
- Acceptable p95 latency: you stated <=200ms; do you have a strict SLA cutoff (e.g., penalty above 250ms) or is it a customer-impact guideline?

If Alex can drop the sample CSV we can run a quick token/latency projection and return a conservative pilot config (we'll include both streaming-optimized and stateless batch variants).

Also attaching the minimal sample schema we need — packly_token_sample.csv (stub).

-Marissa

Sean / Marissa — thanks, þ for the clear list. Quick answers inline and attaching the CSV + short SLA doc: 

- Token distribution: ~95% text-only responses, ~5% include tool calls (pricing lookups) which add ~200 tokens occasionally.
- Burst shape: crests are mix — roughly 70% concurrent small requests (50–150 tokens) across many users, 30% multi-turn sessions that temporarily spike tokens for ~20–60s.
- Sessionization: session_id is sticky per user login and survives short reconnects (we correlate by user_id in the CSV).
- Long-tail: ~7% of requests >500 tokens, ~65% between 60–160 tokens, rest under 60.
- SLA sensitivity: p95 <=200ms is the business bar; customers start to notice >250ms consistently. No hard legal penalty today, but it's a revenue-impact metric for checkout abandonment.

Attached: packly_token_sample.csv (anonymized 72h sample) and packly_mvp_sla.pdf (internal).

We can do the deep-dive on 2026-09-28 10:00 PT — that works for our infra and product folks. For the pilot, curious how Redwood recommends handling the long-tail (>500 token) requests — do you prefer routing them to a different model/quantized profile or to a separate slot to avoid impacting p95?

Thanks — Alex

Alex — perfect, this is exactly what we needed. Quick synthesis and the pilot proposal so we can move to scheduling and procurement: 

Synthesis:
- Baseline/steady-state assumptions: 18–25 rps, avg ~120 tokens/request.
- Peak handling: expect 10–20s crests up to ~30k tokens/sec driven by many concurrent small requests + a minority of large sessions.
- Streaming concurrency: plan for 225 concurrent streams to allow 10% headroom above observed 210.
- Latency target: configure for p95 <= 180–200ms, with a separate guardrail for long-tail (>500 tokens) where best-effort p95 <= 350ms.

Pilot sizing proposal (conservative starting config):
- Dedicated pilot pool equivalent to 4x A100-class GPUs (we'll provide the exact SKU/throughput estimates in the deep-dive).
- Canary ramp: day 1 at 25% traffic, day 2 at 50%, then 100% replay for 48h.
- Routing: long-tail >500 tokens routed to a quantized variant (lower mem footprint) with rate-limits to protect p95 for short requests.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboard, and an automatic rollback on p95 breaches >250ms for 5m windows.

Action items: 
1) Alex: confirm HubSpot deal link / PO owner so procurement can enable trial credits (I dropped the hubspot link above).
2) Packly: drop CSV & SLA (done) — thanks. We'll review and come back with a cost estimate and exact SKU mapping by EOD 2026-09-17.
3) Redwood: Marissa and Karthik will run a quick projection & pilot config after parsing the CSV; we will share a pilot runbook 24h before the deep-dive.

Can we lock the deep-dive for Thu 2026-09-28 10:00 PT? I’ll put a calendar invite with a short agenda (sizing, routing, telemetry, procurement steps).

Sean
